lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The first real Maple Leafs storyline of the fall is already a small lesson in restraint - Gavin McKenna will stay out of the NHL Prospect Challenge and keep training with the big club instead, a sensible call for a teenager with the spotlight already burning hot. Toronto's offseason remains quiet, but not idle; Max Domi's back trouble leaves a hole to monitor, and the Leafs still have a training camp to open with choices to make. McKenna skipping Gatineau to prepare for camp with the NHL group says plenty about the club's priorities - patience, protection, and a push to get him ready for October without forcing the issue. Ben Danford is another name to watch, a steady young defender talking like a player who knows the door is ajar. Toronto finished 2025-26 at 52-26-4, and that kind of record buys nothing now. What matters next is camp - who stays healthy, who sticks, and whether McKenna can turn promise into roster gravity.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and the Blue Jays are already living in the hard light of consequence. Toronto's 7-4 loss to Baltimore only sharpened the questions that matter now: how a club that finished 73-75 keeps from standing still, and whether Trey Yesavage can actually become the arm that changes the shape of the rotation next spring. Scherzer got shelled early, and that only deepens the sense that this staff still needs another layer of certainty. George Springer's recent return to health helps, but a veteran core cannot carry a roster forever. The front office has a winter of heavy lifting ahead. Watch Yesavage's rehab timeline, because if he comes back clean, the offseason suddenly has a spine.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The quiet has a pulse to it now - Toronto's offseason hinges on one pending piece, and it's a big one. Kawhi Leonard's return remains stuck in limbo, even as the league's inquiry into the Clippers has ended, and that uncertainty is shaping everything from the depth chart to the first real look at camp. The Raptors finished last season 39-43, which is why this can't be treated like a luxury; it's roster construction, plain and simple. Leonard is the headline, but the real subplot is who bends the floor around him - Immanuel Quickley, Brandon Ingram, the shooters who make the paint less crowded. Training camp opens Sept. 29 in Quebec City, and that's when the paper roster turns into a real one.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The real story is not the calendar - it's whether Washington's makeover can survive first contact. D.J. Humphries is gone before he ever mattered, a blunt reminder that the line is still a work in progress. That matters because the offense is being asked to carry Jayden Daniels with a patched-together front and new voices calling the shots. The Commanders enter with no games on the board, but plenty of pressure on the blueprint: a rebuilt defense, a bigger target share for Daniels, and a running back room that must hold together. The old comfort of last season is gone. What's left is scrutiny. Watch the offensive line, watch Daniels' protection, and watch whether this summer's fixes look sturdy or flimsy when the real test begins.

article.title: Saturday's Skate
paragraphs: McKenna keeps Leafs in focus, while Ben Danford says he is ready for pro pressure, a useful note for Toronto as camp talk starts to build around the blue line. For the Blue Jays, the wild-card push slipped again in Baltimore, and the morning reads more like a regroup than a rally.

The Raptors are still in deep offseason mode, with their new season plan tied closely to Kawhi Leonard and to finding the right pick-and-roll partners for 2026-27. In Washington, the Commanders are getting an early test of their own, with Jayden Daniels and the offensive line under the microscope as the Eagles wait on the schedule, a reminder that September brings scrutiny even before the games do.
